newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says will stick to tax reform schedule.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says will stick to tax reform schedule.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday he would hold to his planned timetable for passing major tax reforms whether or not cross-party talks with opposition Social Democrats (SPD) reach a compromise.
Waigel said a meeting with the SPD set for Wednesday was not certain to go ahead. "It is not a definite date," he told reporters.

"I can't compel the SPD to come," Waigel added. He restated that the SPD must fundamentally agree to the coalition's tax cutting plans as well as back an overhaul of the social security system for a deal to be possible.

He also said the government was ready in return to go along with SPD demands for reductions in occupational insurance charges this time, even though time was running short to meet the SPD's July deadline.

Waigel was speaking after Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet approved his tax bill for 1999, which would pass the lion's share of a package of 30 billion marks in tax cuts which would be initiated in 1998.

The bill's first reading in the Bundestag lower house of parliament will be held on Friday and Waigel said the measure should clear the Bundestag in June. The SPD can, however, block the measure through its control of parliament's upper house.
